tasks.brief:
Implementation constraints: synchronous, single-threaded, one module-level non-reentrant threading.Lock. Use json, os, shutil, pathlib, logging. Do NOT auto-restore from .bak on load.

Behavioral specification: Fix four defects in the existing storage module. (1) save_snapshot must read the current persisted generation under the lock and pass THAT as expected_revision to the private helper — never pass a constant 0. Sequence: acquire lock, read current generation (missing/unreadable/legacy-list reads as 0), call _save_versioned_snapshot_locked(threads, current), discard returned revision, return None. (2) The load path must accept a top-level JSON list as the legacy primary shape: that list IS the threads, at revision 0. A top-level dict with integer revision >= 0 and threads list is the envelope shape; anything else unreadable follows rule 3. (3) When the primary exists but does not parse as JSON, quarantine it by renaming to <primary-name>.corrupt-<stamp> in the same directory, preserving bytes exactly, then return ([], 0). (4) Remove any automatic .bak fallback on load — only human restore is supported.

Acceptance condition: All storage service tests pass, including legacy list reads, corrupt quarantine, backup rotation failure handling, cleanup failure masking, and revision-advancing saves.

Implementation constraints: FastAPI routes, synchronous handlers. Use pydantic models for validation. Map SnapshotConflict to HTTP 409 with exact JSON body {"error":"revision_conflict", "current_revision": n} — do NOT wrap in FastAPI's detail. Validation failures remain 422 and write nothing.

Behavioral specification: Extend ThreadsPayload with required revision: int >= 0. Add a DELETE body model containing required revision: int >= 0. GET performs one revisioned load and returns {"threads": [...], "revision": n, "quarantined": bool}. PUT calls save_versioned_snapshot(payload.threads, payload.revision); DELETE calls it with []. Both return {"status":"ok", "revision": n+1}. Map SnapshotConflict to HTTP 409 with the exact top-level JSON body {"error":"revision_conflict", "current_revision": n}.

Acceptance condition: All threads API tests pass, including GET empty, PUT/DELETE revision validation (422), revision advancement, stale revision rejection (409), and concurrent same-revision conflict resolution.

Implementation constraints: browser-side JavaScript, no frameworks. Expose minimum hook for app.js to install GET revision before mutations enqueue. Own the authoritative hydrated revision, ordered persist queue, and conflict latch. Run at most one PUT at a time.

Behavioral specification: Every persistence-worthy mutation captures its own complete snapshot at enqueue time. The first request uses the hydrated revision; after a 200, adopt the response revision before issuing the next queued snapshot. Do not coalesce or reorder mutations. Ordinary network/non-409 failures preserve AC-75/AC-76 ("not saved") and do not advance revision. A 409 clears pending snapshots, latches the page against every later PUT/DELETE, and writes exactly "history changed elsewhere — reload required" to save-status. Only document reload clears the latch.

Acceptance condition: Browser persistence conflict tests pass, including rapid mutation serialization, conflict warning and latch, and reload recovery.

Implementation constraints: browser-side JavaScript, no frameworks. During startup GET hydration, install both data.threads and data.revision into the threads persistence owner before rendering or creating state. A healthy reload starts with empty save-status and an unlatch. If GET is empty, default-thread creation is the first queued save against the returned revision. Never infer a revision from content.

A healthy reload starts with empty save-status and an unlatch. If GET is empty, default-thread creation is the first queued save against the returned revision. Never infer a revision from content.

Acceptance condition: All browser UI tests pass, including persistence conflict tests (browser serializes rapid mutations, conflict warns and stops further writes, reload after conflict hydrates and allows new save), plus all carried UI regression tests.
